'''Yuri Mikhailovich Marusik''' ({{langx|ru|Юрий Михайлович Марусик}}; born 13 May 1962) is a Russian [[arachnologist]].

== Early life and education ==
Marusik was born in Sarny, a small town in West Ukraine, to Mikhail Adamovich, a school teacher, and Tamara Andreevna, a nurse. His interest in zoology started at an early age, from reading books about animals.
Marusik started his studies at Leningrad (now [[Saint Petersburg State University|Saint Petersburg]]) State University in 1979 where he specialized in [[entomology]] under the supervision of [[Victor P. Tyshchenko]]. After his graduation in 1984, Marusik was accepted into a [[Ph.D.]] program in [[Magadan]], working in the lab of [[Daniil I. Berman]]. His Ph.D. dissertation (1988) was devoted to [[fauna]], [[Population structure (genetics)|population structure]] and [[spatial distribution]] of [[spiders]] in the upper reaches of the [[Kolyma River]], northeastern [[Siberia]].<ref>{{cite journal | url=https://zookeys.pensoft.net/article/85374/element/5/31// | doi=10.3897/zookeys.1100.85374 | issue=1100 | doi-access=free | title=Forty-two years of scientific research on eight legs—celebrating the 60th birthday of Dr Yuri M. Marusik | journal=ZooKeys | date=13 May 2022 | pages=87–101 | pmid=36760390 | last1=Zhang | first1=J. | last2=Mikhailov | first2=K. G. | last3=Koponen | first3=S. | last4=Long | first4=F. | last5=Yu | first5=H. | last6=Li | first6=S. | pmc=9848612 | bibcode=2022ZooK.1100...87Z }}{{Creative Commons text attribution notice|cc=by4|from this source=yes}}</ref><ref>{{cite web | url=https://mikhail-omelko.com/arachnologists/yuri-marusik/ | title=Yuri Marusik }}</ref>

== Contributions to arachnology ==
Marusik has published over 500 scientific papers dealing with [[taxonomy]], [[systematics]], [[faunistics]] and the [[biogeography]] of spiders and other [[invertebrates]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.researchgate.net/profile/Yuri-Marusik-2|access-date=2023-08-27|title=Yuri M. Marusik}}</ref> He has described two subfamilies and over 50 genera and 700 species of spiders,<ref>{{cite web | url=https://wsc.nmbe.ch/search?sFamily=&fMt=begin&sGenus=&gMt=begin&sSpecies=&sMt=begin&multiPurpose=gAuthor&sMulti=Marusik&mMt=contain&searchSpec=s | title=NMBE - World Spider Catalog }}</ref><ref>{{cite web | url=https://wsc.nmbe.ch/search?sFamily=&fMt=begin&sGenus=&gMt=begin&sSpecies=&sMt=begin&multiPurpose=sAuthor&sMulti=Marusik&mMt=contain&searchSpec=s | title=NMBE - World Spider Catalog }}</ref> several of them named after celebrities: ''[[Filistata maguirei]]'' and ''[[Pritha garfieldi]]'' were named after the former [[Spider-Man]] actors [[Tobey Maguire]] and [[Andrew Garfield]],<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Marusik |first1=Yuri M. |last2=Zamani |first2=Alireza |date=2015 |title=Additional new species of Filistatidae (Aranei) from Iran |url=https://kmkjournals.com/upload/PDF/ArthropodaSelecta/24/24_4_429_435_Marusik_Zamani_for_Inet.pdf |journal=Arthropoda Selecta |volume=24 |issue=4 |pages=429–435|doi=10.15298/arthsel.24.4.05 }}</ref> ''[[Labialithus lindemanni]]'' was named after [[Till Lindemann]], the lead vocalist and lyricist of the band [[Rammstein]],<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.biotaxa.org/Zootaxa/article/view/zootaxa.4899.1.13|title=On two enigmatic spiders (Araneae: Cybaeidae & Phrurolithidae) from the Russian Far East|access-date=2023-08-27}}</ref> ''[[Gorbiscape|Gorbiscape gorbachevi]]'' was named after the Russian and Soviet politician [[Mikhail Gorbachev]],<ref>{{cite journal | url=https://bioone.org/journals/arachnology/volume-18/issue-4/arac.2020.18.4.368/A-review-of-Agelenini-Araneae--Agelenidae--Ageleninae-of/10.13156/arac.2020.18.4.368.short | doi=10.13156/arac.2020.18.4.368 | title=A review of Agelenini (Araneae: Agelenidae: Ageleninae) of Iran and Tajikistan, with descriptions of four new genera | journal=Arachnology | date=March 2020 | volume=18 | issue=4 | pages=368–386 | last1=Zamani | first1=Alireza | last2=Marusik | first2=Yuri M. | s2cid=214702963 | url-access=subscription }}</ref> ''[[Loureedia phoenixi]]'' was named after the actor [[Joaquin Phoenix]],<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.smithsonianmag.com/smart-news/joker-spider-named-after-joaquin-phoenix-180975220/ | title='Joker' Spider Named After Joaquin Phoenix }}</ref> and ''[[Loxosceles coheni]]'' was named after the singer-songwriter, poet and novelist [[Leonard Cohen]].<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.iflscience.com/newtoscience-spider-named-after-leonard-cohen-58115 | title=New-To-Science Spider Named After Leonard Cohen | date=21 December 2020 }}</ref>
